plan: This is a second-price auction (Vickrey-style): I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bidding behavior. Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $30, I will bid exactly $30 to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot auction.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win. Bidding lower reduces my chances of winning without any benefit, since I only pay the second-highest bid anyway. With my value at $6, I should bid $6 to maximize expected profit.
